Realizará trabajos sencillos alrededor de la colonia de una forma incansable y con la máxima dedicación.\n\n<color=#E5E54C>Efecto en el juego:</color>Los constructos acaparan una cantidad de entropía constante en el psíquico que los invoca. Mantener demasiados constructos vivos podría impedir que el psíquico utilize otras habilidades.

Rule.Original: A psychically re-animated husk of a deceased individual. Extremely aggressive, but will soon wither away into nothing.
Rule.Raw: A psychically re-animated husk of a deceased individual. Extremely aggressive, but will soon wither away into nothing.
Rule.Translated: Los restos de una persona fallecida reanimados psíquicamente. Muy agresivo, aunque pronto se convertirá en polvo.
Quizá no todo sea tan malo como pensaba.

Rule.Original: I think things are getting better.
Rule.Raw: I think things are getting better.
Rule.Translated: Creo que las cosas están mejorando.

Rule.Original: Everything is improving, slowly but surely.
Rule.Raw: Everything is improving, slowly but surely.
Rule.Translated: Todo va mejorando, lenta pero inexorablemente.

Rule.Original: I'm feeling good right now, things are looking up.
Rule.Raw: I'm feeling good right now, things are looking up.
Rule.Translated: Me siento tan bien ahora mismo, las cosas están mejorando.

Rule.Original: I feel warm and fuzzy, just being alive feels great.
Rule.Raw: I feel warm and fuzzy, just being alive feels great.
Rule.Translated: Me siento tan a gusto y tan bien... El mero hecho de estar vivo me hace sentir genial.

Rule.Original: I'm just about to burst with excitement. I love this colony, I love this world and all the lives on it.
Rule.Raw: I'm just about to burst with excitement. I love this colony, I love this world and all the lives on it.
Rule.Translated: Estoy a punto de estallar de emoción. ¡Me encanta esta colonia, me encanta este mundo y todos los seres que hay en él!

Rule.Original: All the colors of this world are so vivid, the sounds are so tranquil, the air is so crisp. This life leaves me breathless.
Rule.Raw: All the colors of this world are so vivid, the sounds are so tranquil, the air is so crisp. This life leaves me breathless.
Rule.Translated: Todos los colores de este mundo son tan vivos, los sonidos tan tranquilos, el aire tan fresco. ¡Esta vida me deja sin aliento!

Rule.Original: This is it, isn't it? I've truly reached nirvana itself. Life itself is the very embodiment of happiness.
Rule.Raw: This is it, isn't it? I've truly reached nirvana itself. Life itself is the very embodiment of happiness.
Rule.Translated: Lo he conseguido, ¿verdad...? He conseguido alcanzar el mismísimo nirvana... ¡La vida misma es la encarnación la felicidad...!

Rule.Original: I don’t remember anything, I’m exploring everything anew!
Rule.Raw: I don’t remember anything, I’m exploring everything anew!

Rule.Original: Everyone I knew has changed so much. This timequake really did a number on me.
Rule.Raw: Everyone I knew has changed so much. This timequake really did a number on me.
Rule.Translated: Todas las personas que conocía han cambiado tanto... Este cronosismo sí que me ha fastidiado el día.

Rule.Original: I know my future, and things are looking good!
Rule.Raw: I know my future, and things are looking good!
Rule.Translated: Conozco mi futuro, ¡y las cosas pintan bien!

Rule.Original: Psychic enthrallment caused by incredibly strong mental influence. Thralls don't need to sleep or have recreation, but are unable to do skilled work and engage in social interactions.
Rule.Raw: Psychic enthrallment caused by incredibly strong mental influence. Thralls don't need to sleep or have recreation, but are unable to do skilled work and engage in social interactions.
Rule.Translated: Un estado de embelesamiento psíquico causado por una influencia mental increíblemente fuerte. Los vasallos no necesitan dormir ni divertirse, pero son incapaces de realizar trabajos cualificados y de relacionarse socialmente.

Rule.Original: From 1.5 onwards the advanced animations has been removed from the mod. The Yayo's Animation-mod can be used for this instead as it has the same features. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2877292196
Rule.Raw: From 1.5 onwards the advanced animations has been removed from the mod. The Yayo's Animation-mod can be used for this instead as it has the same features. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2877292196
Rule.Translated: A partir de la versión 1.5, se han retirado las animaciones avanzadas del mod. Puedes utilizar el mod Yayo's Animation para ello, ya que ofrece las mismas funciones. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2877292196

Rule.Original: This update of the mod removes the need for HugsLib, thanks to the help of Zaljerem!
Rule.Raw: This update of the mod removes the need for HugsLib, thanks to the help of Zaljerem!
Rule.Translated: Esta actualización elimina la dependencia de HugsLib gracias a la ayuda de Zaljerem.

Rule.Original: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons.
Rule.Raw: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons.
Rule.Translated: Munición para armas a distancia primitivas y medievales.

Rule.Original: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons. Used for explosion, flame, and smoke damage type weapons.
Rule.Raw: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons. Used for explosion, flame, and smoke damage type weapons.
Rule.Translated: Munición para armas a distancia primitivas y medievales. Se usa en armas que causan daño explosivo, de fuego y de humo.

Rule.Original: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons. Used for special weapons.
Rule.Raw: Ammunition used in primitive and medieval ranged weapons. Used for special weapons.
Rule.Translated: Munición para armas a distancia primitivas y medievales. Se usa en armas especiales.

Rule.Raw: Ammunition used for long-range weapons in the industrial tech.
Rule.Translated: Munición para armas de largo alcance de tecnología industrial.

Rule.Original: A genetically engineered relative of the apatosaurus that now produces explosive chemicals in the sacs on its body. Rule.Original:
The loosely jointed jaws of Allosaurus allow it to open its jaws extremely wide, similar to snakes. While they lack the bone crushing abilities of the Tyrannosaurs, their teeth are very effective at tearing away chunks of flesh as they attack.

Scientific name: Allosaurus fragilis (Fragile different lizard)

The first Allosaurus fossils found were vertebrae, which locals has assumed were petrified horse hooves.

The first Allosaurus fossils found were vertebrae, which locals has assumed were petrified horse hooves.
Rule.Translated:
La articulación flexible de las mandíbulas del Allosaurus le permite abrirlas muchísimo, de forma similar a las serpientes. Aunque no puede triturar huesos como los tiranosaurios, sus dientes arrancan trozos de carne con gran eficacia durante el ataque.

Nombre científico: Allosaurus fragilis (lagarto diferente frágil)

Los primeros fósiles de Allosaurus encontrados eran vértebras que los habitantes locales habían tomado por pezuñas de caballo petrificadas.

Rule.Original:
Relatively small and with a short neck for a sauropod, Amargasaurus has multiple pairs of spines along its neck. Each of the spines is coated in a keratinous sheath, like the horns of an ibex.

While not the easiest animals to manage, their impressive appearance means they command a high price.

Scientific Name: Amargasaurus cazaui (Cazau's lizard of the La Amarga formation)

The exact function of the neck spikes is still debated, with some proposing they supported sails.

Rule.Translated:
Relativamente pequeño y de cuello corto para ser un saurópodo, el Amargasaurus tiene varios pares de espinas a lo largo del cuello. Cada una está cubierta por una vaina de queratina, como los cuernos de un íbice.

Aunque no es fácil de manejar, su aspecto impresionante hace que alcance precios elevados.

Nombre científico: Amargasaurus cazaui (lagarto de Cazau de la formación La Amarga)

La función exacta de las espinas del cuello sigue siendo objeto de debate. Algunos proponen que sostenían velas.

Rule.Original:
Ankylosaurus is perhaps the largest of its kind and has formidible defences, with a thick skull, bony plates covering its back and a collar of bone protecting its neck. If any predators do try to find a gap in its armour the dense club on its tail is more than capable of shattering the bones of large therapods - and the bodies of smaller ones.

Scientific name: Ankylosaurus magniventris (Fused lizard with a wide belly)

There have been relatively few fossils found of Ankylosaurus compared to other related dinosaurs, it owes its fame largely to a scale model of it being displayed at the 1964 World's Fair.
Rule.Raw:
Ankylosaurus is perhaps the largest of its kind and has formidible defences, with a thick skull, bony plates covering its back and a collar of bone protecting its neck. Scientific name: Ankylosaurus magniventris (Fused lizard with a wide belly)

Rule.Translated:
El Ankylosaurus es quizá el mayor de su grupo y cuenta con defensas formidables: un cráneo grueso, placas óseas en el lomo y un collar de hueso que protege el cuello. Si un depredador busca un hueco en su armadura, la densa maza de su cola puede romper los huesos de grandes terópodos y destrozar los cuerpos de los pequeños.

Nombre científico: Ankylosaurus magniventris (lagarto fusionado de vientre ancho)

Se han encontrado relativamente pocos fósiles de Ankylosaurus en comparación con dinosaurios emparentados. Debe gran parte de su fama a una maqueta expuesta en la Feria Mundial de 1964.

Rule.Original:
One of the largest predators of the Permian period, Anteosaurus is not a dinosaur but a synapsid, a mammal-like reptile. While it posesses stout legs and a wide snout like a hippo or crocodile, it is a capable terrestrial hunter.

Scientific Name: Anteosaurus magnificus (Magnificent giant lizard)

Anteosaurus is named after Antaeus, a half-giant slain by Hercules as one of his twelve labours.

Uno de los mayores depredadores del Pérmico, el Anteosaurus no es un dinosaurio, sino un sinápsido: un reptil semejante a los mamíferos. Aunque tiene patas robustas y un hocico ancho como los de un hipopótamo o cocodrilo, es un hábil cazador terrestre.

Nombre científico: Anteosaurus magnificus (magnífico lagarto gigante)

El Anteosaurus recibe su nombre de Anteo, un semigigante al que Hércules mató en uno de sus doce trabajos.

Rule.Original:
Arthropleura, a millipede arthropod, is one of the largest land invertebrates of all time. Though it may look intimidating to those used to the engineered bioweapon insectoids common on the rim, it isn't particularly aggressive and primarily feeds on plants.

Scientific name: Arthropleura armata (Armed jointed ribs)

Most of the fossils of Arthropleura found so far have been shed skins, not the whole animal.

Arthropleura, un artrópodo miriápodo, es uno de los mayores invertebrados terrestres de todos los tiempos. Aunque puede intimidar a quienes conocen los insectoides diseñados como armas biológicas habituales en la frontera, no es especialmente agresivo y se alimenta sobre todo de plantas.

Nombre científico: Arthropleura armata (costillas articuladas armadas)

La mayoría de los fósiles de Arthropleura encontrados hasta ahora son mudas de su cubierta, en lugar del animal completo.

Rule.Original:
A large predatory dinosaur that specializes in hunting fish as well as small to medium prey. With a neck like a pelican it swallows smaller animals whole, larger ones are dismembered with the large claws on its forelimbs.

Scientific name: Baryonyx walkeri (Walker's heavy claw)

The first specimen was found in a clay pit used for making bricks.

The first specimen was found in a clay pit used for making bricks.
Rule.Translated:
Un gran dinosaurio depredador especializado en pescar y cazar presas pequeñas y medianas. Su cuello semejante al de un pelícano le permite tragarse enteros los animales pequeños; desmiembra a los mayores con las grandes garras de sus extremidades delanteras.

Nombre científico: Baryonyx walkeri (garra pesada de Walker)

El primer ejemplar se encontró en una cantera de arcilla destinada a fabricar ladrillos.

Rule.Original:
A relative of Ankylosaurus that lacks a tail club and is considerably calmer. Despite the spikes, these gentle beasts make good pack animals.

Scientific name: Borealopelta markmitchelli (Mark Mitchell's northern shield)

The holotype is remarkably well preserved, and includes not only skin impressions but visible melanocytes indicating that it was red in colour.

Un pariente del Ankylosaurus que carece de maza caudal y es mucho más tranquilo. Pese a las espinas, estas dóciles bestias son buenos animales de carga.

El holotipo está extraordinariamente bien conservado e incluye no solo impresiones de piel, sino melanocitos visibles que indican un color rojo.

Rule.Original:
A huge herbivorous dinosaur. Their long necks are better suited to being held upright than those of other sauropods, in large part due to their body posture, making them efficient defoliators of trees.

Scientific name: Brachiosaurus altithorax (Arm lizard with a deep chest)

As with many dinosaurs excavated during the bone wars, the site where Brachiosaurus was discovered had to be guarded to prevent sabotage and looting.

As with many dinosaurs excavated during the bone wars, the site where Brachiosaurus was discovered had to be guarded to prevent sabotage and looting.
Rule.Translated:
Un enorme dinosaurio herbívoro. Su postura corporal permite mantener el cuello erguido con más facilidad que otros saurópodos, lo que lo convierte en un eficaz consumidor de hojas de árboles.

Nombre científico: Brachiosaurus altithorax (lagarto de brazos con tórax profundo)

Como ocurrió con muchos dinosaurios excavados durante la guerra de los huesos, hubo que vigilar el yacimiento del Brachiosaurus para evitar sabotajes y saqueos.

Rule.Original:
A huge warm blooded herbivore like other sauropods, Camarasaurus specialises in stripping everything even slightly edible from the upper canopy. This tree specific diet allows them to coexist with other sauropods without competition.

Scientific name: Camarasaurus supremus (Supreme chambered lizard)

The name chambered lizard refers to the fact that Camarasaurus has hollow bones like a bird, probably to reduce weight.
Rule.Raw:
A huge warm blooded herbivore like other sauropods, Camarasaurus specialises in stripping everything even slightly edible from the upper canopy. This tree specific diet allows them to coexist with other sauropods without competition.

Scientific name: Camarasaurus supremus (Supreme chambered lizard)

The name chambered lizard refers to the fact that Camarasaurus has hollow bones like a bird, probably to reduce weight.
Rule.Translated:
Un enorme herbívoro de sangre caliente, como otros saurópodos. El Camarasaurus se especializa en arrancar todo lo remotamente comestible de las copas de los árboles. Esa dieta arbórea le permite coexistir con otros saurópodos sin competir.

Nombre científico: Camarasaurus supremus (lagarto con cámaras supremo)

El nombre «lagarto con cámaras» alude a sus huesos huecos semejantes a los de las aves, que probablemente reducen el peso.

Rule.Original:
Carcharodontosaurus is one of the largest land carnivores, and is strong enough to allow it pick up and shake animals as large as horses to death in its mighty jaws.

Scientific name: Carcharodontosaurus saharicus (Great white shark lizard of the sahara).

The first fossils found consisted only of teeth, later found ones were destroyed in an air raid and at last the species was rediscovered for future research.

Nombre científico: Carcharodontosaurus saharicus (lagarto de dientes de tiburón blanco del Sáhara).

Los primeros fósiles encontrados eran solo dientes. Otros restos posteriores quedaron destruidos en un bombardeo y, finalmente, la especie se redescubrió para futuras investigaciones.

Rule.Original:
A large predatory dinosaur named for the distinctive horns above its eyes. It is well adapted for running and has only vestigial arms.

Scientific name: Carnotaurus sastrei (Sastre's Meat eating bull)

Skin impressions have been found alongside Carnotaurus bones, showing it had a wide variety of different scale types.

Se han encontrado impresiones de piel junto a sus huesos que muestran una gran variedad de tipos de escamas.

Rule.Original:
While fairly small for a dinosaur, they live in huge herds making them a dangerous animal to hunt. They are highly variable, with their frills changing shape as they age and having nose horns that can point forwards or backwards depending on the individual.

Scientific name: Centrosaurus apertus (Open pointed lizard)

The name refers to the dinosaur's frill, which has holes in and small spines around the edge. The nose horn was discovered after the animal had been named.

Aunque pequeño para ser un dinosaurio, vive en grandes manadas que lo convierten en una presa peligrosa. Presenta una gran variabilidad: la gola cambia de forma con la edad y el cuerno nasal puede apuntar hacia delante o hacia atrás según el individuo.

Nombre científico: Centrosaurus apertus (lagarto puntiagudo abierto)

El nombre hace referencia a su gola, que tiene aberturas y pequeñas espinas en los bordes. El cuerno nasal se descubrió después de que se diera nombre al animal.

Rule.Original:
The size and shape of its frill make it somewhat unhelpful in defense, instead being used for thermoregulation or display. Like Triceratops, it cares for its young, with juveniles remaining with their parents for extended periods of time.

Scientific name: Chasmosaurus belli (Bell's hollow lizard)

Because the most obvious feature of ceratopsians is their frills, which change over the lifetime of the animal as well as between species, ceratopsian taxonomy is a hotly debated topic with a lot of disagreements.

Rule.Translated:
El tamaño y la forma de su gola la hacen poco útil como defensa; en cambio, sirve para regular la temperatura o exhibirse. Como el Triceratops, cuida de sus crías y los jóvenes permanecen mucho tiempo con los padres.

Nombre científico: Chasmosaurus belli (lagarto hueco de Bell)

Como las golas son el rasgo más evidente de los ceratópsidos y cambian tanto durante la vida del animal como entre especies, su taxonomía provoca intensos debates y numerosos desacuerdos.

Rule.Original:
A small grazing animal with distinctive plates and spikes along its back and tail. These dinosaurs are often found in groups.

Scientific name: Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis (Chongqing lizard of Jiangbei)

The thagomizer is only known from disarticulated fossils, but has been described as a "pin-cushion array".

El conjunto de espinas caudales solo se conoce por fósiles desarticulados, pero se ha descrito como una «disposición de alfiletero».

Rule.Original:
Compsognathus is one of the smaller dinosaur species and like many of their relatives, they are covered in proto-feathers. These tiny predators can run amazingly fast.

Scientific name: Compsognathus longipes (Dainty jaw long legs)

The discovery of Compsognathus changed how people viewed dinosaurs, no longer thinking that they were only giants. They were initially thought to be chicken sized due to the fact that the first fossil discovered was a juvenile.

Nombre científico: Compsognathus longipes (mandíbula delicada de patas largas)

Su descubrimiento cambió la percepción de los dinosaurios y demostró que no todos eran gigantes. Al principio se creyó que tenía el tamaño de una gallina porque el primer fósil era juvenil.

Rule.Original:
Corythosaurus is a large herbivore with sensitive hearing. They are sporadically active throughout the day at short intervals.

Scientific name: Corythosaurus casuarius (Cassowary-like helmet lizard)

They were initially assumed to be aquatic, because the first fossil had been a carcass that had washed up on a beach.

Rule.Original:
Its long fingers are equipped with three large curved claws, but it is the sickle claws on its feet that are its deadliest weapons.

Scientific name: Deinonychus antirrhopus (Counterbalanced terrible claw) 

The discovery of Deinonychus, an active, agile predator, was strong evidence against the previously held assumption that dinosaurs were slow-moving, cold blooded reptiles.

Nombre científico: Deinonychus antirrhopus (garra terrible contrapesada) 

El descubrimiento del Deinonychus, un depredador activo y ágil, fue una prueba contundente contra la antigua idea de que los dinosaurios eran reptiles lentos y de sangre fría.

Rule.Original:
Larger than a bear but far more lightly built and agile, Dilophosaurus is more than capable of preying on humans and livestock; colonists of the rim beware.

Scientific name: Dilophosaurus wetherilli (Wetherill's two-crested lizard)

The cliffs where Dilophosaurus fossils are found are covered in petroglyphs, and their tracks feature in the culture and art of the Navajo.

Nombre científico: Dilophosaurus wetherilli (lagarto de dos crestas de Wetherill)

Los acantilados donde se encuentran sus fósiles están cubiertos de petroglifos y sus huellas aparecen en la cultura y el arte navajos.

Rule.Original:
Dimetrodon have huge heads relative to their body size, giving them a disproportionately strong bite which makes up for their stumpy legs and ineffective claws.

Scientific name: Dimetrodon limbatus (Limbed two measures of teeth)

The function of the sail is still disputed, but whether influenced by the sail or not they most likely had a constant, warm body temperature.

Nombre científico: Dimetrodon limbatus (de extremidades y dientes de dos tamaños)

La función de la vela sigue siendo discutida, pero, dependiera o no de ella, probablemente mantenían una temperatura corporal cálida y constante.

Rule.Original: Dimorphodon is a small pterosaur with a skull nearly one-third of its total body length. Their skull, however, is surprisingly light since it's virtually just scaffolding. It is able to run along the ground using its wings like legs, much like certain bats. The Dimorphodon hunts small prey.\n\nScientific name: Dimorphodon macronyx
Rule.Raw: Dimorphodon is a small pterosaur with a skull nearly one-third of its total body length. Their skull, however, is surprisingly light since it's virtually just scaffolding. It is able to run along the ground using its wings like legs, much like certain bats. The Dimorphodon hunts small prey.\n\nScientific name: Dimorphodon macronyx
Rule.Translated: El Dimorphodon es un pequeño pterosaurio cuyo cráneo representa casi un tercio de su longitud corporal. Sin embargo, el cráneo es sorprendentemente ligero porque prácticamente consiste en una estructura hueca. Puede correr por el suelo utilizando las alas como patas, igual que ciertos murciélagos. Caza presas pequeñas.\n\nNombre científico: Dimorphodon macronyx

Rule.Original:
An amphibian somewhat like a salamander or newt but with a huge boomerang shaped skull.

Scientific name: Diplocaulus salamandroides (Salamader-like double caul)

Some scientists think that its skull shape acted as a hydrofoil, allowing it to move up and down in the water with ease.

Nombre científico: Diplocaulus salamandroides (doble capucha semejante a una salamandra)

Algunos científicos creen que su cráneo actuaba como una superficie sustentadora que le permitía subir y bajar en el agua con facilidad.

Rule.Original:

Rule.Original:

Rule.Original: Known as the “Good Mother” dinosaur, this species lived in large herds and cared for their young after hatching. Their primary defense from predators was running away in herds, making it difficult to be targeted. They began life as primarily bipeds but shifted to primarily quadrupeds as they aged.\n\nScientific name: Maiasaura peeblesorum

Rule.Translated: Conocida como el dinosaurio «buena madre», esta especie vivía en grandes manadas y cuidaba de sus crías tras la eclosión. Rule.Original: Known as the “Tyrant Lizard”, it was a very large predatory dinosaur that was widespread throughout North America. It had an extremely powerful bite force. Rule.Original: One of the most well-known dinosaurs to even the least educated on the Rim, Triceratops had a large neck frill, two large brow horns, and a smaller nasal horn. They sometimes fought among themselves, whether it be for mates or territory and some remains even showed signs of having fought Tyrannosaurs.\n\nScientific name: Triceratops horridus

Rule.Original: It is known from a single partial skeleton, including a partial skull roof and lower jaw, a femur and tibia, part of a rib, and other fragments. Rule.Raw: A large feathered tyrannosaur that lived in colder climates. It was one of the few predators in its environment to have hunted sauropods, with some even having likely died doing so. It had a flat tongue like a crocodile.\n\nScientific name: Yutyrannus huali
Rule.Translated: Un gran tiranosaurio emplumado que vivía en climas fríos. Era uno de los pocos depredadores de su entorno que cazaban saurópodos, y algunos probablemente murieron al hacerlo. Tenía una lengua plana como la de un cocodrilo.\n\nNombre científico: Yutyrannus huali

Rule.Original: A fertilized yutyrannus egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby yutyrannus. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

Rule.Translated: Un huevo fecundado de yutyrannus. Si todo va bien, de él nacerá una cría de yutyrannus. Se puede comer crudo, pero está mucho mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: Closely related to modern octopus and squids, these prehistoric molluscs had curled shells. Due to how common they were on Earth, they make for excellent index fossils. They had a varied diet, from scavenging off the kills of other animals to predating on smaller fish. They are often predated upon by larger sea life.
Rule.Raw: Closely related to modern octopus and squids, these prehistoric molluscs had curled shells. Due to how common they were on Earth, they make for excellent index fossils. Rule.Translated: Emparentados con pulpos y calamares actuales, estos moluscos prehistóricos tenían conchas enrolladas. Su abundancia en la Tierra los convierte en excelentes fósiles guía. Tenían una dieta variada: desde aprovechar los restos de las presas de otros animales hasta cazar peces pequeños. Los grandes animales marinos suelen cazarlos.

Rule.Original: Anomalocaris is one of the earliest examples of an apex predator, feeding on virtually any other animals from its time, often trilobites due to their commonality. It is likely that they used weaknesses in exoskeletal structures to kill their prey, rather than crushing them open, as originally believed. \n\nScientific name: Anomalocaris canadensis
Rule.Raw: Anomalocaris is one of the earliest examples of an apex predator, feeding on virtually any other animals from its time, often trilobites due to their commonality. Rule.Translated: El Anomalocaris es uno de los primeros ejemplos de superdepredador. Comía prácticamente cualquier animal de su época, a menudo trilobites por su abundancia. Probablemente aprovechaba los puntos débiles de los exoesqueletos para matar a sus presas, en lugar de aplastarlos como se creyó inicialmente. \n\nNombre científico: Anomalocaris canadensis

Rule.Original: A gigantic species of cephalopod, once quite common in some areas during the Ordovician period on Earth. It is thought to be largely an ambush predator, lying in wait for its prey rather than actively hunting.\n\nScientific name:Cameroceras trentonense

Rule.Original: On Earth, it was thought to have been extinct for millions of years until nearly the mid 20th century when it was rediscovered as a “living fossil.” It is a poor source of food for humans but is often hunted by larger sea predators.\n\nScientific name: Coelacanthus granulatus

Rule.Original: A heavily armored fish from the late Devonian period, it lacked normal teeth but instead had tooth “plates.” Despite its large size and armoring, it was hunted by other predators of its time.\n\nScientific name: Dunkleosteus terrelli

Rule.Original: Very fast swiming carnivorous hunter which used its long neck to get close to prey without them noticing. A swift flick of the neck could catch them unawares. Its small head limited the size of what it could eat. Scientific name: Elasmosaurus platyurus
Rule.Raw: Very fast swiming carnivorous hunter which used its long neck to get close to prey without them noticing. A swift flick of the neck could catch them unawares. Its small head limited the size of what it could eat. Scientific name: Elasmosaurus platyurus
Rule.Translated: Un cazador carnívoro que nadaba muy rápido y utilizaba su largo cuello para acercarse a las presas sin que lo advirtieran. Un rápido movimiento del cuello podía pillarlas desprevenidas. Su pequeña cabeza limitaba el tamaño de lo que podía comer. Nombre científico: Elasmosaurus platyurus

Rule.Original: Elasmosaurus used its long neck to get close to prey without them noticing. A swift flick of the neck could catch them unawares. Its long, narrow teeth were perfect for piercing and trapping small, soft prey. Scientific name: Elasmosaurus platyurus

Sus dientes largos y estrechos eran perfectos para perforar y atrapar presas pequeñas y blandas. Nombre científico: Elasmosaurus platyurus

Rule.Original: Despite being commonly known as “sea scorpions”, only the earliest forms of Eurypterid were marine, with most of the later ones living in brackish or freshwater. Some may have had dual respiratory systems and may have been able to go on land for short periods of time, like some modern crabs.

Algunos podrían haber tenido sistemas respiratorios dobles y haber podido salir a tierra durante breves periodos, como ciertos cangrejos actuales.

Rule.Original: Closely related to modern octopus and squids, these prehistoric molluscs had curled shells. Due to how common they were on Earth, they make for excellent index fossils. They had a varied diet, from scavenging off the kills of other animals to predating on smaller fish. They are often predated upon by larger sea life. This specific type is larger than most others of its kind.

Rule.Original: A small prehistoric turtle. Its weak legs mean that it spends very little time on land, likely only going on land to lay eggs. It uses baleen in its mouth similar to whales to filter feed.\n\nScientific name:Henodus chelyops

Rule.Original: The Ichthyosaurus may look superficially like a prehistoric dolphin, but Ichthyosaurus was actually an aquatic reptile. Its hands and feet had over time modified into flippers.\n\nScientific name: Ichthyosaurus communis

Rule.Original: Primitive and eel-like, this jawless fish fed primarily upon detritus.\n\nScientific Name:Jamoytius kerwoodi

Rule.Original: The largest of antarctic tylosaurs, it was one of the few large predators in its environment. It likely predates upon anything smaller than it.\n\nScientific Name:Kaikaifilu hervei
Rule.Raw: The largest of antarctic tylosaurs, it was one of the few large predators in its environment. It likely predates upon anything smaller than it.\n\nScientific Name:Kaikaifilu hervei
Rule.Translated: El mayor de los tilosaurios antárticos y uno de los pocos grandes depredadores de su entorno. Probablemente cace cualquier cosa más pequeña que él.\n\nNombre científico:Kaikaifilu hervei

Rule.Original: Despite weighing over one ton, it was actually rather small for a plesiosaur. Its mouth is filled with a multitude of small conical teeth that make it an expert at catching fish.\n\nScientific Name:Kaiwhekea katiki
Rule.Raw: Despite weighing over one ton, it was actually rather small for a plesiosaur. Its mouth is filled with a multitude of small conical teeth that make it an expert at catching fish.\n\nScientific Name:Kaiwhekea katiki
Rule.Translated: A pesar de pesar más de una tonelada, era bastante pequeño para un plesiosaurio. Su boca está llena de multitud de pequeños dientes cónicos que lo convierten en un experto en atrapar peces.\n\nNombre científico:Kaiwhekea katiki

Rule.Original: Kronosaurus was a carnivorous pliosaurs. It had an elongated head, a short neck, a stiff body propelled by four flippers, and a relatively short tail. The posterior flippers were larger than the anterior.\n\nScientific Name:Kronosaurus queenslandicus
Rule.Raw: Kronosaurus was a carnivorous pliosaurs. It had an elongated head, a short neck, a stiff body propelled by four flippers, and a relatively short tail. The posterior flippers were larger than the anterior.\n\nScientific Name:Kronosaurus queenslandicus
Rule.Translated: Kronosaurus era un pliosaurio carnívoro. Tenía una cabeza alargada, un cuello corto, un cuerpo rígido propulsado por cuatro aletas y una cola relativamente corta. Las aletas posteriores eran mayores que las anteriores.\n\nNombre científico:Kronosaurus queenslandicus

Rule.Original: The largest ray-finned fish and one of the largest fish of all time, it was actually a gentle giant of sorts, filtering the water for food instead of hunting down prey.\n\nScientific Name:Leedsichthys problematicus
Rule.Raw: The largest ray-finned fish and one of the largest fish of all time, it was actually a gentle giant of sorts, filtering the water for food instead of hunting down prey.\n\nScientific Name:Leedsichthys problematicus
Rule.Translated: El mayor pez de aletas radiadas y uno de los peces más grandes de todos los tiempos. En realidad era una especie de gigante apacible que filtraba el agua para alimentarse en lugar de perseguir presas.\n\nNombre científico:Leedsichthys problematicus

Rule.Original: A fertilized leedsichthys egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby leedsichthys. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: A fertilized leedsichthys egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby leedsichthys. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo fecundado de leedsichthys. Si todo va bien, de él nacerá una cría de leedsichthys. Se puede comer crudo, pero está mucho mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: An unfertilized leedsichthys egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: An unfertilized leedsichthys egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo sin fecundar de leedsichthys. Se puede comer crudo, pero está muchísimo mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: The Liopleurodon was the apex predator of Europe’s seas during the mid-to-late Jurassic and reached sizes larger than a killer whale. While most plesiosaurs fed on fish and had long necks, Liopleurodon had a shorter neck and a larger head, indicating that it predated on other marine reptiles as well as fish. It is also perfectly willing to eat any unlucky humanoid that is swimming through its domain.\n\nScientific name: L. ferox
Rule.Raw: The Liopleurodon was the apex predator of Europe’s seas during the mid-to-late Jurassic and reached sizes larger than a killer whale. While most plesiosaurs fed on fish and had long necks, Liopleurodon had a shorter neck and a larger head, indicating that it predated on other marine reptiles as well as fish. It is also perfectly willing to eat any unlucky humanoid that is swimming through its domain.\n\nScientific name: L. ferox
Rule.Translated: Liopleurodon era el superdepredador de los mares europeos durante el Jurásico medio y tardío, y alcanzaba tamaños superiores a los de una orca. Mientras que la mayoría de los plesiosaurios comían peces y tenían cuellos largos, Liopleurodon tenía un cuello más corto y una cabeza mayor, lo que indica que también cazaba otros reptiles marinos. Además, no tiene ningún reparo en devorar a cualquier humanoide desafortunado que nade por sus dominios.\n\nNombre científico: L. ferox

Rule.Original: The largest known shark species of all time. Their range covers virtually all warm oceans, with their young living in the warmer shallower waters. They tend to feed upon large prey, such as whales and sea turtles.\n\nScientific name: Otodus megalodon
Rule.Raw: The largest known shark species of all time. Their range covers virtually all warm oceans, with their young living in the warmer shallower waters. They tend to feed upon large prey, such as whales and sea turtles.\n\nScientific name: Otodus megalodon
Rule.Translated: La mayor especie de tiburón conocida de todos los tiempos. Su distribución abarca prácticamente todos los océanos cálidos, y sus crías viven en aguas más cálidas y poco profundas. Suele alimentarse de presas grandes, como ballenas y tortugas marinas.\n\nNombre científico: Otodus megalodon

Rule.Original: Mosasaurus swam using its long crocodile-like body in an undulating motion to swim and devoured all kinds of prey with its massive jaws and sharp, cone-shaped teeth. It lives and hunts the well-lit surface waters of the oceans.\n\nScientific name: Mosasaurus hoffmannii
Rule.Raw: Mosasaurus swam using its long crocodile-like body in an undulating motion to swim and devoured all kinds of prey with its massive jaws and sharp, cone-shaped teeth. It lives and hunts the well-lit surface waters of the oceans.\n\nScientific name: Mosasaurus hoffmannii
Rule.Translated: Mosasaurus nadaba ondulando su largo cuerpo, parecido al de un cocodrilo, y devoraba todo tipo de presas con sus enormes mandíbulas y sus afilados dientes cónicos. Vive y caza en las aguas superficiales bien iluminadas de los océanos.\n\nNombre científico: Mosasaurus hoffmannii

Rule.Original: A distant relative of modern nautilus, these creatures instead have a long conical shell. Their name means “straight horn.”\n\nScientific name: Orthoceras regulare
Rule.Raw: A distant relative of modern nautilus, these creatures instead have a long conical shell. Their name means “straight horn.”\n\nScientific name: Orthoceras regulare
Rule.Translated: Un pariente lejano de los nautilos actuales, aunque estas criaturas tienen una larga concha cónica. Su nombre significa «cuerno recto».\n\nNombre científico: Orthoceras regulare

Rule.Original: A fertilized orthoceras egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby orthoceras. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: A fertilized orthoceras egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby orthoceras. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo fecundado de orthoceras. Si todo va bien, de él nacerá una cría de orthoceras. Se puede comer crudo, pero está mucho mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: An unfertilized orthoceras egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: An unfertilized orthoceras egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo sin fecundar de orthoceras. Se puede comer crudo, pero está muchísimo mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: One of the larger species of ichthyosaur and even one of the largest marine reptiles of all time. They appear to be a relatively specialized offshoot of the main ichthyosaur evolutionary line.\n\nScientific name: Shonisaurus popularis
Rule.Raw: One of the larger species of ichthyosaur and even one of the largest marine reptiles of all time. They appear to be a relatively specialized offshoot of the main ichthyosaur evolutionary line.\n\nScientific name: Shonisaurus popularis
Rule.Translated: Una de las especies de ictiosaurios más grandes y uno de los mayores reptiles marinos de todos los tiempos. Parece ser una rama relativamente especializada del linaje evolutivo principal de los ictiosaurios.\n\nNombre científico: Shonisaurus popularis

Rule.Original: While comparable in size to modern crocodilians, this species instead had a streamlined and finned body suited for the open ocean. Like many other aquatic predators, it had "salt glands" that allowed it to filter out the salt from the water it ingests as well as its salty prey.\n\nScientific Name:Metriorhynchus brevirostris
Rule.Raw: While comparable in size to modern crocodilians, this species instead had a streamlined and finned body suited for the open ocean. Like many other aquatic predators, it had "salt glands" that allowed it to filter out the salt from the water it ingests as well as its salty prey.\n\nScientific Name:Metriorhynchus brevirostris
Rule.Translated: Aunque su tamaño era comparable al de los cocodrilos actuales, esta especie tenía un cuerpo hidrodinámico con aletas, adaptado al mar abierto. Como muchos otros depredadores acuáticos, tenía «glándulas salinas» que le permitían filtrar la sal del agua que ingería y de sus presas saladas.\n\nNombre científico:Metriorhynchus brevirostris

Rule.Original: A fertilized thalattosuchus egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby thalattosuchus. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: A fertilized thalattosuchus egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby thalattosuchus. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo fecundado de thalattosuchus. Si todo va bien, de él nacerá una cría de thalattosuchus. Se puede comer crudo, pero está mucho mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: An unfertilized thalattosuchus egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: An unfertilized thalattosuchus egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo sin fecundar de thalattosuchus. Se puede comer crudo, pero está muchísimo mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: Trilobites were one of the most common arthropods on the planet, with as much if not more variety in diet, habitat, and size than modern crabs. They survived in one form or another from the early Cambrian to the end of the Permian. Because of their wide diversity and an easily fossilized exoskeleton, they left extensive fossil records.
Rule.Raw: Trilobites were one of the most common arthropods on the planet, with as much if not more variety in diet, habitat, and size than modern crabs. They survived in one form or another from the early Cambrian to the end of the Permian. Because of their wide diversity and an easily fossilized exoskeleton, they left extensive fossil records.
Rule.Translated: Los trilobites eran uno de los artrópodos más comunes del planeta, con tanta o más variedad de dietas, hábitats y tamaños que los cangrejos actuales. Sobrevivieron de una forma u otra desde el Cámbrico temprano hasta el final del Pérmico. Su gran diversidad y un exoesqueleto que se fosilizaba fácilmente hicieron que dejaran un extenso registro fósil.

Rule.Original: A fertilized trilobite egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby trilobite. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: A fertilized trilobite egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby trilobite. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo fecundado de trilobite. Si todo va bien, de él nacerá una cría de trilobite. Se puede comer crudo, pero está mucho mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: An unfertilized trilobite egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Raw: An unfertilized trilobite egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
Rule.Translated: Un huevo sin fecundar de trilobite. Se puede comer crudo, pero está muchísimo mejor cocinado.

Rule.Original: A small animal build nest, for holding eggs. Egg-laying animals will lay eggs in the nests if they can. The nest also protects eggs from deteriorating outdoors, though it does not protect from temperature damage.
Rule.Raw: A small animal build nest, for holding eggs. Egg-laying animals will lay eggs in the nests if they can. The nest also protects eggs from deteriorating outdoors, though it does not protect from temperature damage.
Rule.Translated: Un pequeño nido construido por animales para guardar huevos. Los animales ovíparos pondrán sus huevos en los nidos si pueden. El nido también impide que los huevos se deterioren al aire libre, aunque no los protege de los daños por temperatura.

Rule.Original: A large animal build nest for holding eggs. Egg-laying animals will lay eggs in the nests if they can. The nest also protects eggs from deteriorating outdoors, though it does not protect from temperature damage.
Rule.Raw: A large animal build nest for holding eggs. Egg-laying animals will lay eggs in the nests if they can. The nest also protects eggs from deteriorating outdoors, though it does not protect from temperature damage.
Rule.Translated: Un gran nido construido por animales para guardar huevos. Los animales ovíparos pondrán sus huevos en los nidos si pueden. El nido también impide que los huevos se deterioren al aire libre, aunque no los protege de los daños por temperatura.

Rule.Original: Lightweight, thin leather from a small dinosaur. Doesn't insulate well.
Rule.Raw: Lightweight, thin leather from a small dinosaur. Doesn't insulate well.
Rule.Translated: Cuero fino y ligero de un dinosaurio pequeño. No aísla bien.

Rule.Original: Medium dinosaur hide, often from dinosaurs with few natural defenses.
Rule.Raw: Medium dinosaur hide, often from dinosaurs with few natural defenses.
Rule.Translated: Piel de dinosaurio de grosor medio, normalmente de dinosaurios con pocas defensas naturales.

Rule.Original: Heavy hide from larger, tougher dinosaurs. It's reasonbly good at protection.
Rule.Raw: Heavy hide from larger, tougher dinosaurs. It's reasonbly good at protection.
Rule.Translated: Piel gruesa de dinosaurios grandes y resistentes. Ofrece una protección bastante buena.

Rule.Original: Armored hide from a bulky dinosaur. Protects quite well.
Rule.Raw: Armored hide from a bulky dinosaur. Protects quite well.
Rule.Translated: Piel acorazada de un dinosaurio corpulento. Protege bastante bien.

Rule.Original: Leather from a feathery dinosaur. Not very protective, but insulates well due to being covered by a soft down. It is also quite pretty.
Rule.Raw: Leather from a feathery dinosaur. Not very protective, but insulates well due to being covered by a soft down. It is also quite pretty.
Rule.Translated: Cuero de un dinosaurio emplumado. No protege demasiado, pero aísla bien gracias al suave plumón que lo recubre. También es bastante bonito.

Rule.Original: Dark chitin from a prehistoric creature. Blades tend to glance off of it.
Rule.Raw: Dark chitin from a prehistoric creature. Blades tend to glance off of it.
Rule.Translated: Quitina oscura de una criatura prehistórica. Las hojas de las armas tienden a resbalar sobre ella.

Rule.Original: Soft, light and provides very good insulation. Cloth made from them can keep the body warm even in very cold conditions.
Rule.Raw: Soft, light and provides very good insulation. Cloth made from them can keep the body warm even in very cold conditions.
Rule.Translated: Suaves y ligeras, ofrecen un aislamiento excelente. La tela hecha con ellas mantiene el cuerpo caliente incluso con mucho frío.

Rule.Original: Just the most beautiful parts of a chromatic dino.
Rule.Raw: Just the most beautiful parts of a chromatic dino.
Rule.Translated: Solo las partes más hermosas de un dinosaurio cromático.

Rule.Original: Pine nuts supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Nice to eat, even when raw.
Rule.Raw: Pine nuts supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Nice to eat, even when raw.
Rule.Translated: Los piñones aportan mucha energía alimentaria y son una fuente rica en numerosos micronutrientes. Son agradables de comer, incluso crudos.

Rule.Original: cycad nuts supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Their roots and seeds are often populated by bacteria known to produce a neurotoxin.
Rule.Raw: cycad nuts supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Their roots and seeds are often populated by bacteria known to produce a neurotoxin.
Rule.Translated: Las semillas de cícada aportan mucha energía alimentaria y son una fuente rica en numerosos micronutrientes. Sus raíces y semillas suelen albergar bacterias que producen una neurotoxina.

Rule.Original: Fern spores supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Nice to eat, even when raw.
Rule.Raw: Fern spores supply high amounts of food energy and are a rich source of numerous micronutrients. Nice to eat, even when raw.
Rule.Translated: Las esporas de helecho aportan mucha energía alimentaria y son una fuente rica en numerosos micronutrientes. Son agradables de comer, incluso crudas.

Rule.Original: A raptors razor-sharp sickle claw. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Raw: A raptors razor-sharp sickle claw. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Translated: La garra en forma de hoz y afilada como una cuchilla de un raptor. Un auténtico trofeo y un arma cuerpo a cuerpo mortal.

Rule.Original: An ceratopsia's horn. It is very durable but mostly hollow. While somewhat complicated to wield as a melee weapon, it can be used quickly and deadly.
Rule.Raw: An ceratopsia's horn. It is very durable but mostly hollow. While somewhat complicated to wield as a melee weapon, it can be used quickly and deadly.
Rule.Translated: El cuerno de un ceratopsio. Es muy resistente, aunque está casi hueco. Si bien resulta algo complicado manejarlo como arma cuerpo a cuerpo, puede utilizarse con rapidez y resultar letal.

Rule.Original: A tyrannosaurus skull. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Raw: A tyrannosaurus skull. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Translated: Un cráneo de tyrannosaurus. Un auténtico trofeo.

Rule.Original: A dilophosaurus skull. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Raw: A dilophosaurus skull. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Translated: Un cráneo de dilophosaurus. Un auténtico trofeo.

Rule.Original: A spinosaurus sail. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Raw: A spinosaurus sail. This is a true trophy.
Rule.Translated: Una vela dorsal de spinosaurus. Un auténtico trofeo.

Rule.Original: A saurumbo blade feather. It's razor-sharp, rock-hard, and priceless in most markets. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Raw: A saurumbo blade feather. It's razor-sharp, rock-hard, and priceless in most markets. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Translated: Una pluma afilada de saurumbo. Es tan cortante como una cuchilla, dura como una roca y de un valor incalculable en la mayoría de los mercados. Es un auténtico trofeo, además de un arma cuerpo a cuerpo letal.

Rule.Original: The blade-sharp part of the bladecrest's head. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Raw: The blade-sharp part of the bladecrest's head. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.
Rule.Translated: La parte de la cabeza del bladecrest afilada como una hoja. Un auténtico trofeo y un arma cuerpo a cuerpo mortal.

Rule.Original: Superficially resembling an ear of wheat, this plant is actually one of the earliest vascular plants.
Rule.Raw: Superficially resembling an ear of wheat, this plant is actually one of the earliest vascular plants.
Rule.Translated: Aunque parece una espiga de trigo, esta planta es en realidad una de las primeras plantas vasculares.
Una conífera primitiva de poca altura.

Rule.Original: A primitive seed fern which yields edible nuts.
Rule.Raw: A primitive seed fern which yields edible nuts.
Rule.Translated: Un helecho primitivo con semillas que produce frutos secos comestibles.

Rule.Original: While comparable in size to some tree ferns, the giant fern is entirely leaves and produces no wood.
Rule.Raw: While comparable in size to some tree ferns, the giant fern is entirely leaves and produces no wood.
Rule.Translated: Aunque tiene un tamaño comparable al de algunos helechos arborescentes, el helecho gigante es todo hojas y no produce madera.

Rule.Original: A softwood tree that grows very fast. Predates both monkeys and puzzles.
Rule.Raw: A softwood tree that grows very fast. Predates both monkeys and puzzles.
Rule.Translated: Un árbol de madera blanda que crece muy rápido. Es anterior tanto a los monos como a los rompecabezas.

Rule.Original: In addition to producing wood, the tulip tree is beautiful with its white, beetle polinated flowers.
Rule.Raw: In addition to producing wood, the tulip tree is beautiful with its white, beetle polinated flowers.
Rule.Translated: Además de producir madera, el tulípero destaca por sus hermosas flores blancas polinizadas por escarabajos.

Rule.Original: A small perennial wildflower that grows in alpine climates.
Rule.Raw: A small perennial wildflower that grows in alpine climates.
Rule.Translated: Una pequeña flor silvestre perenne que crece en climas alpinos.

Rule.Original: Once considered the earliest known tree, it produces spores rather than seeds.
Rule.Raw: Once considered the earliest known tree, it produces spores rather than seeds.
Rule.Translated: Considerado en su día el árbol más antiguo conocido, produce esporas en lugar de semillas.

Rule.Original: An early plant that has root-like branches. While it looks like it has leaves, its “leaves” are actually just protrusions.
Rule.Raw: An early plant that has root-like branches. While it looks like it has leaves, its “leaves” are actually just protrusions.
Rule.Translated: Una planta primitiva con ramificaciones similares a raíces. Aunque parece tener hojas, sus «hojas» no son más que protuberancias.

Rule.Original: A spiky tropical bush with edible fruit.
Rule.Raw: A spiky tropical bush with edible fruit.
Rule.Translated: Un arbusto tropical espinoso con frutos comestibles.

Rule.Original: A temperate-biome tree known for its thin, white, paper-like bark.
Rule.Raw: A temperate-biome tree known for its thin, white, paper-like bark.
Rule.Translated: Un árbol de biomas templados conocido por su corteza fina, blanca y semejante al papel.

Rule.Original: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Un arbusto de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Raw: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Translated: Musgo silvestre que crece en grupos en zonas con poca luz y temperaturas frescas. Tarda mucho en crecer, pero es muy resistente a las heladas.

Rule.Original: A fast growing giant horsetail. It doesn't yield as much usable wood as other trees.
Rule.Raw: A fast growing giant horsetail. It doesn't yield as much usable wood as other trees.
Rule.Translated: Una cola de caballo gigante de crecimiento rápido. No produce tanta madera aprovechable como otros árboles.

Rule.Original: The woody nature of associated stalks and preserved short shoots are evidence that caytoniales were seasonally deciduous, shrubs and trees.
Rule.Raw: The woody nature of associated stalks and preserved short shoots are evidence that caytoniales were seasonally deciduous, shrubs and trees.
Rule.Translated: La naturaleza leñosa de los tallos asociados y los brotes cortos conservados indica que las caytoniales eran arbustos y árboles de hoja caduca estacional.

Rule.Original: An elegant tree with cascading leaves and high quality wood.
Rule.Raw: An elegant tree with cascading leaves and high quality wood.
Rule.Translated: Un árbol elegante de hojas colgantes y madera de gran calidad.

Rule.Original: Shrubby stands of clubmoss. They grow in clusters and slow down movement.
Rule.Raw: Shrubby stands of clubmoss. They grow in clusters and slow down movement.
Rule.Translated: Matas arbustivas de licopodios. Crecen en grupos y ralentizan el movimiento.

Rule.Original: Tough, woody ferns with large lobed leaves. Thorn-bracken grows in clusters, and slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Raw: Tough, woody ferns with large lobed leaves. Thorn-bracken grows in clusters, and slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Translated: Helechos duros y leñosos con grandes hojas lobuladas. Los helechos espinosos crecen en grupos y ralentizan a quien los atraviesa.

Rule.Original: Cooksonia. Slows down anyone moving over it.
Rule.Raw: Cooksonia. Slows down anyone moving over it.
Rule.Translated: Cooksonia. Ralentiza a quien pasa por encima.

Rule.Original: Adult crinoids are called sea lilies and are attached to the sea bottom by a stalk. While they may appear to be a plant, they are actually an animal, much like sea anemone.
Rule.Raw: Adult crinoids are called sea lilies and are attached to the sea bottom by a stalk. While they may appear to be a plant, they are actually an animal, much like sea anemone.
Rule.Translated: Los crinoideos adultos se llaman lirios de mar y están sujetos al fondo marino por un pedúnculo. Aunque parezcan plantas, en realidad son animales, como las anémonas de mar.

Rule.Original: A short shruby cycad. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short shruby cycad. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Una cícada arbustiva de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: Tall clustered ferns. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Raw: Tall clustered ferns. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Translated: Helechos altos agrupados. Ralentizan a quien los atraviesa.

Rule.Original: Wild dicroidium. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Raw: Wild dicroidium. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Translated: Dicroidium silvestre. Crece donde haya algo de luz y un suelo mínimamente fértil.

Rule.Original: Commonly known as umbrella ferns, the earliest species showed up during the Triassic period.
Rule.Raw: Commonly known as umbrella ferns, the earliest species showed up during the Triassic period.
Rule.Translated: Conocidos como helechos paraguas, sus primeras especies aparecieron durante el Triásico.

Rule.Original: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones.
Rule.Raw: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones.
Rule.Translated: Una gran conífera cubierta de piñas espinosas.

Rule.Original: Tough fibrous vegetation that produces a variety of exciting chemicals.
Rule.Raw: Tough fibrous vegetation that produces a variety of exciting chemicals.
Rule.Translated: Vegetación dura y fibrosa que produce diversas sustancias químicas estimulantes.

Rule.Original: Tough fibrous vegetation that produces a variety of exciting chemicals.
Rule.Raw: Tough fibrous vegetation that produces a variety of exciting chemicals.
Rule.Translated: Vegetación dura y fibrosa que produce diversas sustancias químicas estimulantes.

Rule.Original: Raw cut leaves of a ephedra. Can be refined into various form of the stimulant drug psychite.
Rule.Raw: Raw cut leaves of a ephedra. Can be refined into various form of the stimulant drug psychite.
Rule.Translated: Hojas crudas de efedra recién cortadas. Pueden refinarse en varias formas de la droga estimulante psicoide.

Rule.Original: Recently chew ephedra. I am awake.
Rule.Raw: Recently chew ephedra. I am awake.
Rule.Translated: Ha masticado efedra recientemente. Estoy despierto.

Rule.Original: I can do this all day.
Rule.Raw: I can do this all day.
Rule.Translated: Puedo hacer esto todo el día.

Rule.Original: the silver apricot tree. Its fruits are weakly poisonous.
Rule.Raw: the silver apricot tree. Its fruits are weakly poisonous.
Rule.Translated: El árbol del albaricoque plateado. Sus frutos son ligeramente venenosos.

Rule.Original: Long considered a fern after its discovery, it was later assigned to the gymnosperms. But its relationships with other groups remain obscure.
Rule.Raw: Long considered a fern after its discovery, it was later assigned to the gymnosperms. But its relationships with other groups remain obscure.
Rule.Translated: Tras su descubrimiento se consideró durante mucho tiempo un helecho, pero más tarde se clasificó entre las gimnospermas. Sin embargo, su relación con otros grupos sigue sin estar clara.

Rule.Original: A primitive seed fern which yields edible nuts.
Rule.Raw: A primitive seed fern which yields edible nuts.
Rule.Translated: Un helecho primitivo con semillas que produce frutos secos comestibles.

Rule.Original: A fern with that produces tubers too bitter to eat, but that can be used to make a basic antiseptic.
Rule.Raw: A fern with that produces tubers too bitter to eat, but that can be used to make a basic antiseptic.
Rule.Translated: Un helecho que produce tubérculos demasiado amargos para comer, pero útiles para fabricar un antiséptico básico.

Rule.Original: Known as horn corals due to their unique shape, they were once quite common in prehistoric seas.
Rule.Raw: Known as horn corals due to their unique shape, they were once quite common in prehistoric seas.
Rule.Translated: Conocidos como corales cuerno por su peculiar forma, eran muy comunes en los mares prehistóricos.

Rule.Original: Wild horsetail, while nutritionally comparable to grasses, their high silicon content makes them difficult to digest. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Raw: Wild horsetail, while nutritionally comparable to grasses, their high silicon content makes them difficult to digest. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Translated: La cola de caballo silvestre tiene un valor nutritivo comparable al de las gramíneas, pero su alto contenido en silicio dificulta su digestión. Ralentiza a cualquiera que camine sobre ella.

Rule.Original: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Raw: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Translated: Hierba silvestre. Crece donde haya algo de luz y un suelo mínimamente fértil.

Rule.Original: Wild horsetail, while nutritionally comparable to grasses, their high silicon content makes them difficult to digest. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Raw: Wild horsetail, while nutritionally comparable to grasses, their high silicon content makes them difficult to digest. Slows down anyone moving over them.
Rule.Translated: La cola de caballo silvestre tiene un valor nutritivo comparable al de las gramíneas, pero su alto contenido en silicio dificulta su digestión. Ralentiza a cualquiera que camine sobre ella.

Rule.Original: An ancient medium-sized tree, easily identifiable by its distinct scaled trunk.
Rule.Raw: An ancient medium-sized tree, easily identifiable by its distinct scaled trunk.
Rule.Translated: Un antiguo árbol mediano, fácilmente reconocible por su característico tronco escamoso.

Rule.Original: Crawling fern greatly slows down anyone who moves over it.
Rule.Raw: Crawling fern greatly slows down anyone who moves over it.
Rule.Translated: El helecho rastrero ralentiza mucho a quien lo atraviesa.

Rule.Original: The wicker fern are the earliest-known gymnosperms.
Rule.Raw: The wicker fern are the earliest-known gymnosperms.
Rule.Translated: Los helechos de mimbre son las gimnospermas más antiguas conocidas.

Rule.Original: A bushy plant with large pointed leaves to divert rainwater during tropical storms.
Rule.Raw: A bushy plant with large pointed leaves to divert rainwater during tropical storms.
Rule.Translated: Una planta frondosa de grandes hojas puntiagudas que desvían el agua de lluvia durante las tormentas tropicales.

Rule.Original: A short tree-like seed fern with a soft stem that yields no wood.
Rule.Raw: A short tree-like seed fern with a soft stem that yields no wood.
Rule.Translated: Un helecho con semillas, de poca altura y aspecto arbóreo, cuyo tallo blando no produce madera.

Rule.Original: The trunks of Meriani had a distinctive segmented, bamboo-like appearance and vertical ribbing, but were made of wood.
Rule.Raw: The trunks of Meriani had a distinctive segmented, bamboo-like appearance and vertical ribbing, but were made of wood.
Rule.Translated: Los troncos de Meriani tenían un aspecto segmentado similar al bambú y estrías verticales, pero eran de madera.

Rule.Original: The shortest of the ancient redwoods.
Rule.Raw: The shortest of the ancient redwoods.
Rule.Translated: La más baja de las secuoyas antiguas.

Rule.Original: Aquatic plants with disk shaped leaves and huge, beautiful flowers. Unable to support the weight of humans or dinosaurs.
Rule.Raw: Aquatic plants with disk shaped leaves and huge, beautiful flowers. Unable to support the weight of humans or dinosaurs.
Rule.Translated: Plantas acuáticas de hojas discoidales y flores enormes y hermosas. No soportan el peso de humanos ni dinosaurios.

Rule.Original: A palm of wet areas that produces no usable wood, but has sugar-rich stems that can be used to brew alcohol.
Rule.Raw: A palm of wet areas that produces no usable wood, but has sugar-rich stems that can be used to brew alcohol.
Rule.Translated: Una palmera de zonas húmedas que no produce madera útil, pero cuyos tallos ricos en azúcar permiten elaborar alcohol.

Rule.Original: A palm of wet areas that produces no usable wood, but has sugar-rich stems that can be used to brew alcohol.
Rule.Raw: A palm of wet areas that produces no usable wood, but has sugar-rich stems that can be used to brew alcohol.
Rule.Translated: Una palmera de zonas húmedas que no produce madera útil, pero cuyos tallos ricos en azúcar permiten elaborar alcohol.

Rule.Original: Raw nypa. A flavoring and preserving agent that is necessary for making beer.
Rule.Raw: Raw nypa. A flavoring and preserving agent that is necessary for making beer.
Rule.Translated: Nypa cruda. Un agente aromatizante y conservante necesario para elaborar cerveza.

Rule.Original: A lover of damp environments, comb ferns thrive in the humid environment of tropical swamps.
Rule.Raw: A lover of damp environments, comb ferns thrive in the humid environment of tropical swamps.
Rule.Translated: Amantes de los ambientes húmedos, los helechos peine prosperan en los pantanos tropicales.

Rule.Original: A type of seed fern that was once extremely common in the American continents.
Rule.Raw: A type of seed fern that was once extremely common in the American continents.
Rule.Translated: Un tipo de helecho con semillas que fue extremadamente común en los continentes americanos.

Rule.Original: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones. It grows in a distinctive conical shape.
Rule.Raw: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones. It grows in a distinctive conical shape.
Rule.Translated: Una gran conífera cubierta de piñas espinosas. Crece con una característica forma cónica.

Rule.Original: Pleuromeia was an herbaceous plant that lacks secondary tissues and had an unbranched stem.
Rule.Raw: Pleuromeia was an herbaceous plant that lacks secondary tissues and had an unbranched stem.
Rule.Translated: Pleuromeia era una planta herbácea sin tejidos secundarios y con un tallo sin ramificaciones.

Rule.Original: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Un arbusto de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: A hardwood tree. Takes a long time to grow, but their wood is strong.
Rule.Raw: A hardwood tree. Takes a long time to grow, but their wood is strong.
Rule.Translated: Un árbol de madera dura. Tarda mucho en crecer, pero su madera es resistente.

Rule.Original: Wild tall grass. Slows down anyone moving over it.
Rule.Raw: Wild tall grass. Slows down anyone moving over it.
Rule.Translated: Hierba alta silvestre. Ralentiza a quien la atraviesa.

Rule.Original: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Raw: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Translated: Musgo silvestre que crece en grupos en zonas con poca luz y temperaturas frescas. Tarda mucho en crecer, pero es muy resistente a las heladas.

Rule.Original: A tiny yellow flower which grows in large clusters. Though it is often considered a weed, five fingers in bloom are quite beautiful.
Rule.Raw: A tiny yellow flower which grows in large clusters. Though it is often considered a weed, five fingers in bloom are quite beautiful.
Rule.Translated: Una diminuta flor amarilla que crece en grandes grupos. Aunque a menudo se considera una mala hierba, la cincoenrama resulta muy bonita cuando florece.

Rule.Original: A type of plant known only from fossils from the upper Devonian period of Earth.
Rule.Raw: A type of plant known only from fossils from the upper Devonian period of Earth.
Rule.Translated: Un tipo de planta conocido solo por fósiles del Devónico superior de la Tierra.

Rule.Original: Tangled masses of cord-like, spiky vines which coil in great masses along the ground. Chokevine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it. Multiple tribes have independently generated stories of chokevine strangling children to death in the night, as a way to scare kids into coming home before dark.
Rule.Raw: Tangled masses of cord-like, spiky vines which coil in great masses along the ground. Chokevine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it. Multiple tribes have independently generated stories of chokevine strangling children to death in the night, as a way to scare kids into coming home before dark.
Rule.Translated: Masas enmarañadas de enredaderas espinosas, parecidas a cuerdas, que se enrollan formando grandes marañas sobre el suelo. La enredadera estranguladora ralentiza mucho a cualquiera que la atraviese. Varias tribus han creado de forma independiente historias en las que estas enredaderas estrangulan a niños por la noche, para asustarlos y hacer que vuelvan a casa antes del anochecer.

Rule.Original: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Raw: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.
Rule.Translated: Musgo silvestre que crece en grupos en zonas con poca luz y temperaturas frescas. Tarda mucho en crecer, pero es muy resistente a las heladas.

Rule.Original: A rose plant which yields delicious berries. Berries can be cooked, but they're also good to eat even when raw.
Rule.Raw: A rose plant which yields delicious berries. Berries can be cooked, but they're also good to eat even when raw.
Rule.Translated: Una planta de la familia de las rosas que produce bayas deliciosas. Pueden cocinarse, pero también están buenas crudas.

Rule.Original: An unusual plant with tall, pretty flowers. One of the first buttercups.
Rule.Raw: An unusual plant with tall, pretty flowers. One of the first buttercups.
Rule.Translated: Una planta inusual de flores altas y bonitas. Uno de los primeros ranúnculos.

Rule.Original: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Raw: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
Rule.Translated: Hierba silvestre. Crece donde haya algo de luz y un suelo mínimamente fértil.

Rule.Original: A sturdy tree covered in protective scales. Despite its high yield it is not ideal for wood production due to the time it takes to get through the tree's armour.
Rule.Raw: A sturdy tree covered in protective scales. Despite its high yield it is not ideal for wood production due to the time it takes to get through the tree's armour.
Rule.Translated: Un árbol resistente cubierto de escamas protectoras. A pesar de su elevado rendimiento, no es ideal para producir madera debido al tiempo necesario para atravesar su armadura.

Rule.Original: A short ginkgo shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short ginkgo shrub. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Un arbusto de ginkgo de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: Tangled masses of cord-like vines which coil in great masses along the ground. The leaves are thick and tough and difficult to brush aside. Fanvine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it.
Rule.Raw: Tangled masses of cord-like vines which coil in great masses along the ground. The leaves are thick and tough and difficult to brush aside. Fanvine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it.
Rule.Translated: Masas enmarañadas de enredaderas parecidas a cuerdas que se enrollan formando grandes marañas sobre el suelo. Sus hojas son gruesas y duras, y cuesta apartarlas. La enredadera abanico ralentiza mucho a cualquiera que la atraviese.

Rule.Original: These microorganisms produce adhesive compounds that cement sand and other rocky materials to form mineral "microbial mats". In turn, these mats build up layer by layer, growing gradually over time.
Rule.Raw: These microorganisms produce adhesive compounds that cement sand and other rocky materials to form mineral "microbial mats". In turn, these mats build up layer by layer, growing gradually over time.
Rule.Translated: Estos microorganismos producen compuestos adhesivos que cementan arena y otros materiales rocosos para formar «tapetes microbianos» minerales. A su vez, estos tapetes se acumulan capa a capa y crecen gradualmente con el tiempo.

Rule.Original: The vegetative parts of the plant and its seeds are very poisonous. The arillus, on the other hand, is non-toxic and can be eaten. After eating several "berries" including seeds, a doctor should be consulted. The toxin is called taxine and contains, among other things, the diterpene taxol.
Rule.Raw: The vegetative parts of the plant and its seeds are very poisonous. The arillus, on the other hand, is non-toxic and can be eaten. After eating several "berries" including seeds, a doctor should be consulted. The toxin is called taxine and contains, among other things, the diterpene taxol.
Rule.Translated: Las partes vegetativas de la planta y sus semillas son muy venenosas. El arilo, en cambio, no es tóxico y se puede comer. Si se ingieren varias «bayas» con sus semillas, se debe consultar a un médico. La toxina se llama taxina y contiene, entre otras cosas, el diterpeno taxol.

Rule.Original: A short teraxylopteris. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short teraxylopteris. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Un teraxylopteris de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: A fast-growing tree-like plant that grows in dense groves. Bamboo can be harvested for a wood-like material. The plant itself is not beautiful.
Rule.Raw: A fast-growing tree-like plant that grows in dense groves. Bamboo can be harvested for a wood-like material. The plant itself is not beautiful.
Rule.Translated: Una planta similar a un árbol que crece rápidamente y forma densos bosquetes. El bambú puede cosecharse para obtener un material parecido a la madera. La planta en sí no es bonita.

Rule.Original: A short fern. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Raw: A short fern. Does not typically talk.
Rule.Translated: Un helecho de poca altura. No suele hablar.

Rule.Original: For some glitterworld artists, animals are merely another canvas. It's unclear what (if anything) the artist behind the chromatic ankylosaur was trying to say, except perhaps that dangerous animals in crazy colours are rad.

Rule.Translated: Para algunos artistas de los mundos relucientes, los animales son un lienzo más. No está claro qué intentaba expresar el creador del anquilosaurio cromático, si es que intentaba expresar algo, salvo quizá que los animales peligrosos con colores disparatados molan.

Rule.Original: A unfertilized chromatic ankylosaurus egg. Beautiful to look at.
